title: Editing: one module owns when Editing ends
lede: The Editing rule ("Escape or pressing anywhere else ends it") used to be enforced by each caller, in 7 places across 5 files. Now callers only **report what happened** (`startEditing`, `pressed`, `escaped`, `deleted`) and the pure transitions in `src/ui/editing.ts` **decide whether Editing ends**, through one private `end`, and record why. Behaviour doesn't change; this is the single exit #41 will save its Draft text at.

files.question: When does Editing end?
files.summary: Pure transitions over `{ editingId, editingEndedBy }`; every ending goes through `end`, which records the reason.
files.owns: At most one Note in Editing, which events end it, and why it last ended.
files.never: Touches the DOM: focus, caret and blur stay in `Note`.
files.tested: Node tests in `src/ui/uiStore.test.ts`, through the ui store's actions, including that a no-op leaves the state reference the same.

files.question: How do callers reach Editing?
files.summary: Four actions, each one `set` of an Editing transition; the state carries `editingId` and `editingEndedBy`.
files.owns: The public interface of Editing, next to the Current colour and Undo.
files.never: Decides anything about Editing itself: that is `editing.ts`.

files.question: What does a Note report, and how does it react?
files.summary: Presses, keyboard focus and Escape are reported unconditionally; focus goes back to the article only when Editing ended by Escape.
files.owns: The DOM side: caret placement, refocus after Escape, and ignoring an Escape that cancelled a Drag.
files.never: Checks whether it is the edited Note before reporting: the module does.
files.tested: The existing `editing`, `keyboard` and `drag` browser tests, unchanged.

files.question: What does a press on empty Board do?
files.owns: Telling an empty-Board press from one on a Note.

files.question: What does a delete tell Editing?
files.summary: `deleteNote` reports `deleted(id)`, then records Undo, then removes the Note.
files.owns: The order of the cross-store update.
files.never: Checks which Note is being edited: `deleted` does.
files.tested: `notesActions.test.ts`: deleting another Note keeps Editing, deleting the edited one ends it.

steps.title: pointerdown on Note b while Note a is in Editing
steps.explain: `press` reports the press without asking whether this Note is the edited one. Before, it called `stopEditing` only `if (!editing)`: the rule lived here.

steps.title: The ui store runs the transition
steps.explain: One `set`: a transition that returns its input leaves the state reference the same, so Zustand notifies nobody.

steps.title: The module decides: b isn't the edited Note, so Editing ends
steps.explain: `end` is the only place Editing ends. It records `'press'`; #41 will save the Draft text here.

steps.title: Note a re-renders without its textarea
steps.explain: `useIsEditing(a)` flips, the textarea unmounts and focus leaves it. That is why the explicit blur in `useStopEditing` could go: all browser tests pass in Chromium and Firefox without it. `editingEndedBy` is `'press'`, so a doesn't take focus.

scenarios.name: Escape, and the Escape that cancels a Drag

steps.title: keydown Escape in the textarea
steps.explain: If the Drag engine prevented it (it cancelled a Drag), nothing is reported and Editing stays on. Otherwise `escaped()`.

steps.title: The article takes focus after the textarea is gone
steps.explain: `wasEditing` tells a real ending from a Note that mounts idle (e.g. one brought back by Undo while an old `'escape'` is still recorded). So Tab carries on from this Note.

steps.title: pointerdown on empty Board while not Editing
steps.explain: The Board reports `pressed(null)` without checking anything; with no Note in Editing, `end` returns the state unchanged, so nobody is notified.

steps.title: A press on the edited Note's own Grip strip
steps.explain: `pressed(a)` while a is edited returns the same state: no notify, no re-render, Editing stays on. Covered by the test "a press on the edited Note keeps Editing".

steps.title: Deleting a Note that isn't being edited
steps.explain: `deleteNote` always reports; `deleted` ends Editing only for that Note.

notes.title: `deleted(id)` instead of a generic `end(reason)`
notes.detail: The issue sketched `end(reason)` for delete and `pagehide`. Deleting a Note that isn't edited must not end Editing, so the module needs the id: `deleted(id)` keeps that decision inside. #41 adds its own event for `pagehide`.

notes.title: `startEditing` keeps its name
notes.detail: On the ui store a bare `start` would be ambiguous next to Undo and the Current colour, and keeping it leaves most tests untouched. It now goes through `end` when another Note is being edited.

notes.title: `pressed` also covers keyboard focus
notes.detail: Focus arriving on another Note already ended Editing; it is reported as `pressed(id)`, though the glossary's Press is a pointer going down. Counter-argument: a separate name (`focused`) would say it more exactly but behave identically.

notes.title: One browser test line changed
notes.detail: `colours.browser.test.tsx` ended Editing with `stopEditing()`, which no longer exists; it now reports `pressed(null)`, a press on empty Board.

notes.title: Only `'escape'` is read today
notes.detail: `'press'` and `'delete'` are recorded for the tests and for #41.
